sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the review page
sections.what: Brings in icons, navigation, the button, the review card and the layout card.

sections.name: initialMeds
sections.title: Sample medicines list
sections.what: Three sample medicines with the name read from the report, a cleaned name, dosage, timing and a confidence score.
sections.why: Likely reason: stands in for real extraction results during early building.
sections.watch_out: These are not the user's medicines. They must be replaced by real results before use.

sections.name: OCRReviewPage (part 1)
sections.title: Editing, deleting and approving
sections.what: Holds the medicine list in the page. Editing merges changes into one item and deleting removes it. Approve shows a saving message, waits 1.5 seconds, then goes to the dashboard.
sections.why: Lets the user correct the list before it is final. The wait is marked in the code as a simulated API call.
sections.watch_out: Approve never sends data to the backend, so the change is lost when the page is left.

sections.name: OCRReviewPage (part 2)
sections.title: Medicine cards and action buttons
sections.what: Lists each medicine as an editable card, shows a Cancel and Discard button and an Approve and Update Schedule button. Also shows a side panel with the source file name and a note about automatic scheduling.
sections.why: Gives the user a clear choice between keeping and throwing away the extracted list.
sections.watch_out: The side panel promises that approved medicines will be added automatically, which the code does not do yet.

summary: The screen where a user checks medicines the app read from a report, edits or removes them, and approves the list before it is meant to update the schedule.
purpose: Gives the user a final check on extracted medicines so mistakes from the scanner do not reach their schedule.
why: Reading handwritten or printed reports is error-prone, so a human check is built in before saving.
how: The page starts with sample medicines. Each card can edit or delete an item, which changes the list in memory. Approve waits about 1.5 seconds and then goes to the dashboard. No data is sent to the backend in the current code.
inputs: The sample medicine list defined in the file, and the user's edits and clicks.
outputs: A list of confirmed medicine entries on screen, and a move to the dashboard after approve. Nothing is saved.
risks: The approval does not save anything, so the user may believe the schedule was updated when it was not. The sample medicines are shown instead of the real extraction. The source file name is fixed text.
debug: If approved medicines do not appear on the dashboard, this is expected, because approve only simulates a save. To check real behavior, look for the backend call that should replace the setTimeout and confirm the list is sent.
